name: Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe
evidence_rating: thin: Commission self-evaluation and audit evidence on co-funding; no counterfactual study of impact for the Horizon Europe JUs
summary: This regulation set up nine public-private research partnerships (aviation, rail, hydrogen, chips, health and others) meant to multiply EU research money with industry funds. The Commission's 2025 mid-term review finds they attract co-funding and support strategic technologies, but few newcomers join and only some speed up market uptake. EU auditors report sizeable shortfalls in promised partner contributions for several of them.

indicators.objective: The proposal's LFS has no indicators (1.4.4 lists synergies); partnerships are monitored under Articles 45 and 47 and Annex III of the Horizon Europe Regulation and feed into Horizon Europe interim and ex-post evaluations
Leverage of private and national funding
indicators.indicator: Non-EU contributions mobilised per EU euro (e.g. KDT/Chips 1:3 leverage)
indicators.target_or_baseline: EU EUR 17.2bn to leverage EUR 21.3bn (123%) in 2021-2027
indicators.evidence: ECA: planned leverage lower than 2014-2020 (158%); shortfalls for some JUs - Global Health EDCTP3 partners' cash only EUR 15.6m (4% of EUR 400m target) by end-2024; SESAR 3/Eurocontrol and IHI also short. HE interim evaluation: JU projects have highest direct leverage factor (0.8) among HE actions.

indicators.indicator: Scientific, economic and technological impacts of partnerships
indicators.evidence: HE interim evaluation: partnerships contributed to new knowledge and EU leadership in key technologies; only a smaller number of JUs had an impact on accelerating uptake of innovative solutions. Based on partnership evaluations, not counterfactual.

indicators.indicator: New members; SME and widening-country participation
indicators.evidence: 308 new organisations joined partnerships 2022-2024, mostly EIT KICs; few newcomers in JUs; only three JUs have SMEs as members; about 15% of JU funding went to SMEs.

indicators.objective: Sector targets (e.g. aviation emissions, rail, hydrogen, health)
indicators.evidence: Too early; no ex-post measures of sector outcomes found. Predecessor (Horizon 2020) JUs covered in SWD(2024) 29.

literature.citation: European Commission (2021), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Council Regulation establishing the Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe (executive summary SWD(2021) 38), SWD(2021) 37
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Council Regulation establishing the Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe (executive summary SWD(2021) 38)
literature.method: ex-ante (coordinated IA of 9 partnerships; option comparison)
literature.headline: Institutionalised partnerships preferred for each area; e.g. Key Digital Technologies expected leverage of 1:3 (EUR 1 EU, EUR 1 states, EUR 2 private) with SMEs at least one-third of participants; aviation and rail options with over 60% of costs covered by private partners
literature.summary_plain: The Commission argued that public-private joint undertakings would multiply EU research money with industry and national funds, e.g. three extra euros for every EU euro in chips research.

literature.citation: European Commission (2025), Interim Evaluation of the Horizon Europe Framework Programme 2021-2024 (incl. annexes on 19 institutionalised partnerships), SWD(2025) 110
literature.title: Interim Evaluation of the Horizon Europe Framework Programme 2021-2024 (incl. annexes on 19 institutionalised partnerships)
literature.headline: JUs have highest direct leverage (0.8; EU covers 55% of eligible costs); older partnerships leverage much more than newer ones; impacts on knowledge and value-chain resilience, but only some JUs accelerated uptake of innovations; few newcomers; SMEs members in only three JUs
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's mid-term review finds the joint undertakings bring in co-funding and help strategic technologies, but few newcomers join and only some speed up market uptake.

literature.citation: European Court of Auditors (2025), Annual report on EU joint undertakings for the 2024 financial year, ECA annual report
literature.title: Annual report on EU joint undertakings for the 2024 financial year
literature.headline: Planned 2021-2027 leverage (123%) lower than 2014-2020 (158%); by end of Horizon 2020 period members met 96% of contribution targets on average but with shortfalls (SESAR 3, IHI, EuroHPC); Global Health EDCTP3 at 4% of contributing-partner target
literature.summary_plain: EU auditors find the joint undertakings' finances sound overall, but several are well short of the private or partner money they promised.

literature.title: Annual report on EU Joint Undertakings for the financial year 2023
literature.venue: European Court of Auditors, annual report on JUs (published 2024)
literature.method: annual financial and compliance audit of all JUs: substantive testing of grant payments, extrapolated error rates, and tracking of member contributions against founding-regulation targets
literature.outcomes: JU budget execution, private members' in-kind contributions vs targets, error rates in grant payments
literature.headline: By end-2023 JUs had reached 94% of their Horizon 2020 member contribution targets overall but EuroHPC only 45%, with EuroHPC private members reporting just €18.4 million of in-kind contributions against a €420 million target; estimated average error rate for 2023 grant expenditure was just below the 2% materiality threshold.
literature.summary_plain: The EU auditors signed off the joint undertakings' 2023 accounts, but found that private industry partners in some of them, especially the supercomputing one, are paying in far less than promised. Mistakes in grant payments were close to the acceptable limit.
literature.period_geography: Financial year 2023; EU (11 JUs incl. those set up under Regulation 2021/2085)
literature.quality: Independent audit with hard financial data; focuses on legality, regularity and contribution targets rather than research outcomes; earlier edition of the FY2024 report already listed.
literature.citation: European Court of Auditors (2024), Annual report on EU Joint Undertakings for the financial year 2023, European Court of Auditors, annual report on JUs (published 2024)

literature.authors: European Commission, Directorate-General for Research and Innovation (Unit G4, Common Missions & Partnerships Service)
literature.title: Performance of European Partnerships: Biennial Monitoring Report 2024 on partnerships in Horizon Europe
literature.venue: Publications Office of the EU, doi:10.2777/991766
literature.method: monitoring report with descriptive statistics on 44 European Partnerships (incl. the Art. 187 JUs) from eCORDA grant data and partnerships' self-reported leverage and KPI data
literature.outcomes: leverage of private/other funding, success rates, participation, KPIs of institutionalised partnerships
literature.headline: Institutionalised partnerships (JUs, excl. KICs) show total direct leverage of 1.44 euro per EU euro but indirect leverage of only 0.20, which the report says means JU outcomes do not yet trigger substantial follow-on investment.
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's own monitoring of its research partnerships finds that the industry-led joint undertakings bring in about 1.4 euros of partner money for every EU euro, but so far spark little further investment to take results to market.
literature.period_geography: Horizon Europe 2021-2023 data; EU27 plus associated countries
literature.quality: Rich administrative data but leverage figures are self-reported and early in programme life (report flags reliability caveats); Commission monitoring its own programme; descriptive.
literature.citation: European Commission, Directorate-General for Research and Innovation (Unit G4, Common Missions & Partnerships Service) (2024), Performance of European Partnerships: Biennial Monitoring Report 2024 on partnerships in Horizon Europe, Publications Office of the EU, doi:10.2777/991766
